moves.name: Avião
moves.description: Peak-energy figure (Zouk1 band 4). The dZouk curriculum lists an 'avião'.

moves.name: Passo Básico Atrás
moves.description: The slow-quick-quick basic danced backward.

moves.name: Bônus
moves.description: A travelling turn in which the leader steps behind the follower instead of in front; she turns about one and a half times and ends facing her start direction, and the weight transfer makes a pause in the basic. The left bonus ends with a patinha ('little paw', a back step with inverted footwork). Hands stay joined (AmoZouk); the version where the leader lets go is the boomerang.

moves.name: Bumerangue
moves.description: The no-hands relative of the bônus (AmoZouk): the leader lets go and the follower travels past and comes back like a boomerang. One source treats boomerang as the European name for bônus; Zouk1 keeps both (Boomerang -> Bonus), which matches AmoZouk's split.

moves.name: Cambré
moves.description: A controlled backbend extending the whole spine while the follower stays supported; forum users call cambrés 'the dips'. Variants: forward cambré, sitting cambré. Maps best onto Dip Back; the three 'Dip' nodes and Fall Back may be other cambré shapes (see hypotheses).

moves.name: Giro Duplo
aliases: Giro Duplo para os Dois Lados
moves.description: Two follower rotations.

moves.name: Passo Básico à Frente
moves.description: The slow-quick-quick basic danced forward (passo básico frente e trás = forward and back).

moves.name: Gostosinho
moves.description: A comfortable hug at the end of a back-and-forth basic. In Zouk1 it follows Back Basic, which matches.

moves.name: Abraço
moves.description: The closed embrace position; the grounded hub of the Zouk1 graph (10 outgoing links).

moves.name: Corredor
moves.description: The basic side-to-side travelling pattern: the follower walks back and forth along a line past the leader and turns 180 degrees with a compass step at each end; her hips point along the line while her chest stays turned to the leader (torso torsion). Usually entered from a viradinha. Two sources (a salsaforums post and Helen Avelar's 'LATERAL/CORREDOR' tutorial) treat corredor and lateral as one move; the user decided on 2026-10-06 that Lateral is renamed Corredor.

moves.name: Giro no Eixo
moves.description: Fast follower spin on one foot.

moves.name: Giro Invertido
aliases: Giro Invertido com a Mão Direita

moves.name: Preparação para Giro
moves.description: A preparatory side step with the weight on one leg, used to enter turns. Side Lunge is the main hub of Zouk1 (14 inbound links, out to the turns), which fits. Open Lunge and Step To Side are other candidates.

moves.name: Giro Simples
moves.description: The basic follower turn. 'giro' is the generic Portuguese word for turn.

moves.name: Soltinho
aliases: Giro do Cavalheiro e da Dama
moves.description: Leader and follower take turns turning while orbiting a shared circle; a single-foot turn on a fixed axis.

moves.name: Viradinha
moves.description: The follower makes a 180-degree backward pivot on the ball of the foot (a compass step) and goes back the way she came; led mainly with the leader's chest, his hand behind her shoulder. It is the entry into the corredor/lateral. 'veraginha' is how the Brazilian pronunciation (di = 'dji') sounds.

moves.name: Ioiô
moves.description: The follower makes a travelling turn in towards the leader, then out the other way. Isolated in Zouk1: see proposed_links.

moves.name: Balanço
moves.description: An angled basic of three steps forward or back, inherited from lambada.

moves.name: Balão
moves.description: Head movement: the upper body circles around a vertical axis.

moves.name: Bate cabelo
moves.description: Figure-8 upper-body motion with a relaxed neck so the hair whips.

moves.name: Boneca
moves.description: A lambazouk head/upper-body movement, often led visually.

moves.name: Chicote
moves.description: Head accent: the follower throws her hair back while looking up as an accent (timing 'count 1 or 5, prepared forward on 8' is unverified); common in lambazouk. May be what the user calls 'Howl Up' (head thrown back, looking up) and is a candidate for 'cicada' - see hypotheses and unresolved_aliases.

moves.name: Contrapeso
moves.description: The leader anchors the follower's support foot at one point and walks a full circle around her at arm's length; both lean away and hold each other in tension (shared centre of mass between them). Researched name: contrapeso (the pivot itself is a planada); the pião is a different move (both rotate in closed frame).

moves.name: Frango assado
moves.description: Head movement: the upper body rotates around a horizontal axis.

moves.name: Pião
moves.description: In closed frame, leader and follower both rotate around a central axis between them; head movement can be added. A counterbalanced pião is the closed-frame relative of the Contrapeso pivot. Not in Zouk1 (Hug Simple Turn is the nearest node; ask the user whether it is the same).

moves.name: Sarrada
moves.description: Hip-led press against the partner in close embrace. The user identified the move first heard as 'cicada' as sarrada (2026-10-06); the terminology research found no zouk syllabus source, so the name rests on the user's decision.

moves.name: Toalha
moves.description: Head movement while turning with her back to the leader.

Hourglass.label: holds / embraces / isolations
Hourglass.evidence_note: the names also include falls and drags, and turns started from the embrace (the yellow hourglasses)

Diamond.label: steps and basics
Diamond.evidence_note: the names also include step-driven figures: small turns (viradinha), lunges, splits, dips

Tetra.label: head movements (howls) and dips
Tetra.evidence_note: the names also include behind-the-follower / overhead positions (gostosinho, reposition behind, overhead springload)

Ball.label: special wave moves
Ball.evidence_note: yoyo, do the wave, plus overhead/reverse specials

blue.evidence_note: embraces, holds, tilts, stands, open break, hand positions

yellow.evidence_note: mostly turns and pirouettes, plus leg split and drag

orange.evidence_note: the top of the graph: downswing, fast pirouette

legend.note: Shape and tone meanings as confirmed by the user on 2026-10-06 (VIEWER_SPEC 3.10). agreement = share of named nodes of that shape whose authored name fits the meaning; exceptions and evidence_note are evidence only. Corrections go in taxonomy/additions.toml ([legend] table).

energy: energy = (y - y_range[0]) / (y_range[1] - y_range[0]); bands equal-width in energy

display.note: suggested viewer placement (VIEWER_SPEC 3.10): position + offset centres the graph on the origin with its lowest node 0.2 m above the floor; positions themselves stay as authored
